title: Assistant Management Accountant
description:
Assistant Finance Business Partner

Lincoln Manufacturing Sector

£35,000-£45,000 per annum + Benefits.

Ready to take your finance career beyond the numbers?

A leading manufacturing business in Lincoln is looking for an ambitious Assistant Finance Business Partner to join their growing finance team. This is an excellent opportunity for a commercially minded finance professional who wants to play a key role in supporting operational decision-making, driving business performance, and partnering with stakeholders across the organisation.

If you're looking to move away from purely transactional finance and gain genuine exposure to business partnering within a fast-paced manufacturing environment, this could be the perfect next step.

Key responsibilities include:
- Supporting month-end reporting and management accounts preparation

- Experienced in a finance analyst, assistant management accountant, assistant finance business partner, or similar role
- Comfortable analysing financial data and translating it into meaningful business insights
- Confident communicating with stakeholders at all levels
- Proactive, curious, and keen to develop their commercial finance skills
- Advanced in Excel and comfortable working with large datasets

In return, you'll benefit from:

Exposure to senior decision-makers and commercial projects

Clear progression towards a Finance Business Partner role

Support with professional qualifications

Competitive salary and benefits package

Flexible working arrangements

The opportunity to influence business performance within a successful manufacturing environment

If you're ready to accelerate your finance career and join a business where your insights genuinely make a difference, we'd love to hear from you.

Apply today or contact us for a confidential discussion about this exciting Assistant Finance Business Partner opportunity based in Lincoln.

Don't miss the chance to be part of a business that values commercial thinking, continuous improvement, and career development.

title: Assistant Management Accountant
description:
Assistant Management Accountant

Lincoln Study Support Career Development

Are you looking to develop your accounting career in a role that offers genuine exposure beyond transactional finance?

We are recruiting an Assistant Management Accountant for an established and forward-thinking organisation based in Lincoln. This is an excellent opportunity for someone who has gained some practical finance experience and now wants to develop their management accounting skills while working towards an AAT, ACCA or CIMA qualification with study support.

Working closely with the Finance Manager and wider finance team, you'll initially take responsibility for a mixture of transactional and month-end accounting, with the opportunity to broaden your responsibilities as you develop.

Your role will include:
- Supporting the month-end close and preparation of management information
- Preparing and posting journals, accruals and prepayments
- Completing balance sheet and cash reconciliations
- Investigating variances and ensuring financial information is accurate
- Supporting cashflow reporting and wider financial analysis
- Processing supplier invoices and assisting with payment runs
- Maintaining accurate general ledger records and audit trails
- Assisting with year-end reporting and tax information
- Working with the wider finance team to improve systems and processes
- Identifying opportunities to automate tasks and reduce manual processes

We're looking for someone with previous accounts or finance experience who is keen to progress. You may currently be working as an Accounts Assistant, Finance Assistant, Assistant Accountant or part-qualified Management Accountant.

You'll need good attention to detail, strong Excel skills and, importantly, the confidence to ask questions and suggest better ways of doing things.

Alongside professional study support, the role offers 24 days' holiday plus bank holidays, a good employer pension, discretionary bonus, and excellent benefits.

If you're ambitious, enjoy learning and want a role where your responsibilities can grow alongside your accounting career, apply now for a confidential discussion.

Role Responsibilities

The Post Completion Paralegal in Spalding, Lincolnshire will take ownership of a varied caseload following completion of residential property transactions. Key responsibilities will include:
- Managing a caseload of post completion files from completion through to registration and closure
- Preparing and submitting Stamp Duty Land Tax returns and arranging payment where required
- Preparing, submitting and progressing applications to HM Land Registry
- Reviewing and responding to Land Registry requisitions within the relevant timescales
- Serving leasehold notices and dealing with certificates of compliance, restrictions and other title requirements
- Checking post completion documentation and maintaining accurate case management records
- Liaising with fee earners, lenders, managing agents, freeholders and other relevant parties to progress matters
- Closing files once all post completion requirements have been satisfied
- Reporting to a senior member of the property team and escalating complex issues appropriately

Person Specification

You will have practical experience of residential conveyancing post completion work and be comfortable managing competing deadlines. You should also be able to demonstrate the following:
- Experience managing a caseload of post completion files
- Knowledge of Stamp Duty Land Tax submissions and HM Land Registry applications
- An accurate and methodical approach to documents, records and deadlines
- Strong organisation and prioritisation skills
- Clear written and verbal communication skills
- The ability to work independently while contributing to a dedicated team
- Confidence using case management systems and standard Microsoft Office applications
- The ability to work full time from the firm's office in Spalding, Lincolnshire

Benefits and Rewards

This office based Post Completion Paralegal job in Spalding, Lincolnshire offers a competitive package and access to the firm's wider wellbeing benefits. The successful Post Completion Paralegal will also benefit from:
- A salary of £26,000 to £28,000 dependent on experience
- Free Parking
- Private health insurance for all employees

- Group life assurance of up to three times salary
- 25 days annual leave excluding bank holidays with the opportunity to buy and sell additional days
- Access to a 24-hour employee assistance programme and clinically trained mental health experts
- Access to trained Mental Health First Aiders
- Discounted legal fees following one year's employment
- Paid volunteering leave to support the local community
- Summer and Christmas social events
- Training, development and career progression opportunities

About the Law Firm

This extremely well established, multi-site regional law firm supports private individuals and businesses across a broad range of legal services. It offers a collaborative working culture, places training and development at the heart of its approach and provides opportunities for people to grow within the firm.

Next Steps

Apply now to be considered for this new Post Completion Paralegal opportunity in Spalding Lincolnshire. Alternatively, for a confidential discussion about this Post Completion Paralegal job, please send your CV to Izzie Vaughan at the Eventus Recruitment Group for a confidential discussion. description:
SF Recruitment are currently recruiting for a Credit Controller to join a well-established business based in Grantham on a fixed-term maternity cover contract. This is a key role within the Finance team, managing a portfolio of B2 B customers across multiple business entities, with a strong focus on aged debt and overdue balances.
- Salary: £30,000pa
- Contract: Fixed-term maternity cover
- Location: Grantham
- Working pattern: Monday to Thursday 9:00am-5:30pm, Friday 9:00am-5:00pm
- Working arrangement: Fully office-based

The role
Working alongside another Credit Controller, you will take responsibility for managing outstanding customer balances, maintaining accurate Sales Ledger records and building strong relationships with customers to resolve queries and minimise overdue debt. This is a predominantly B2 B Credit Control role, with a particular emphasis on aged debt and proactively managing overdue accounts.

There is also an exciting opportunity to support the implementation of an integrated Credit Control solution, working to help improve and streamline the existing credit control process.

The role will include:

Credit Control & Aged Debt
- Proactively monitor customer balances and chase overdue debt in line with internal processes.
- Manage a portfolio of B2 B customer accounts, ensuring outstanding balances are followed up promptly.
- Escalate overdue accounts to management and regional managers where appropriate.
- Work with legal consultants where required to support the recovery of problematic debt.

Sales Ledger & Reporting
- Maintain accurate and up-to-date Sales Ledger records across multiple business entities.
- Ensure customer accounts are kept tidy, accurate and reconciled.
- Produce weekly aged debt reports and attend regular internal debt meetings.
- Maintain accurate customer information within the accounting system.
- Carry out appropriate credit checks for new customers.

Customer Relationships
- Manage the Sales Ledger customer email inboxes, responding to queries professionally and promptly.
- Build effective working relationships with customers and internal teams to resolve queries and facilitate payment.
- Investigate and resolve issues that may be preventing outstanding invoices from being paid.

Systems & Process Improvement
- Support the Management Accountant with the implementation of the newCredit Control solution.
- Identify opportunities to improve the efficiency and effectiveness of existing Credit Control processes.
- Utilise accounting software and Microsoft Excel to manage customer information, reporting and debt.

About you:
We are looking for an experienced Credit Controller who is confident managing overdue B2 B debt.
You will need strong communication skills, good attention to detail and the ability to manage your own workload.

The successful candidate will be proactive, personable and organised, with the confidence to work independently while contributing effectively to the wider Finance team.
If you are an experienced Credit Controller looking for a new interim opportunity in Grantham, we'd be keen to hear from you.

Please apply now or contact SF Recruitment for more information.

You will require excellent communication, organisational and IT skills, as well as having an exemplary telephone manner, with the initiative to work on your own at times. Lincolnshire Talking Therapies is a successful service that provides a stepped care model for the treatment of people with mild to moderate mental health problems. For further information please contact Pamela Dennis, Team Manager, Skegness LTT via email at Pamela.dennis6@nhs.net We are not able to offer sponsorship for this role. Please provide details of the visa type and expiry date in your application. Failure to provide the required information will result in your application being rejected. As an Administrator, you will play a crucial role in supporting the smooth operation of our talking therapies service. You'll assist both clinical and non-clinical teams, ensure a welcoming environment for all visitors, and develop essential skills for a future NHS career. To undertake reception and routine administration duties in support of clinical and non-clinical activity, ensuring a professional and efficient reception service is provided for all visitors, including service users, carers, contractors, external and internal stakeholders, along with site colleagues and teams. Main Duties of the Apprentice Administrator (Mental Health NHS Talking Therapies): - Provide administrative support to the talking therapies team, including answering phones and responding to emails. - Assist with booking appointments, managing waiting lists, and scheduling assessments. - Maintain accurate and confidential patient records in line with NHS policies. - Welcome and guide service users, families, and visitors to the service. - Support the preparation and distribution of clinical documents, letters, and reports. - Help to organise meetings and take minutes when required. - Input data and generate routine reports for the team. - Work closely with clinical and administrative colleagues to ensure the smooth running of the service. - Uphold patient confidentiality and treat all information sensitively. - Undertake general office tasks such as photocopying, scanning, and filling Please view the attached Job Description and Person Specification for further details regarding this position.

title: Receptionist
description: The GP receptionist is responsible for undertaking a wide range of reception duties and providing support to the multidisciplinary team. Duties may include, but are not limited to, greeting and directing patients, effective use of the appointment system, booking appointments, processing of personal information and assisting patients as required. To act as a central point of contact for patients, the distribution of information, messages and enquiries for the clinical team, liaising with the multidisciplinary team member and external agencies such as secondary care and community service providers. The core responsibilities of the receptionist are as follows. On occasion, there may be a requirement to carry out tasks not listed below, that are within the reasonable scope of the role. Maintain and monitor practice appointment system Process personal, telephone and e-requests for appointments Answer incoming phone calls, dealing with the callers request appropriately Signpost patients to the correct service Initiating contact with and responding to, requests from patients, team members and external agencies Data entry of new and temporary registrations and relevant patient information as requested Input data as necessary onto patients healthcare records Direct requests for information to relevant team members i.e., SAR, DVLA forms, insurance/solicitors letters Manage all queries as necessary in an efficient manner Carry out system searches as requested Support all clinical staff with general tasks as required Photocopy documentation as required Maintain a clean, tidy and effective working area Monitor and maintain the reception area and notice boards In addition to the core responsibilities, the Receptionist may be requested to; 1. Action incoming emails and correspondence as necessary 2. Complete opening and closing procedures in accordance with the rota 3. Partake in audit as directed by the audit lead 4. Support admin team, providing cover during absences 5. Scan patient related documents and attach scanned documents to patients healthcare record We currently have 2 part time vacancies available allowing us to be flexible for the right candidate. All hours will be worked between 08:00 and 18:30, Monday to Friday

title: Care Navigator / Receptionist
description: Spilsby Surgery is looking for a friendly, enthusiastic and reliable Care Navigator / Receptionist to join our busy and supportive team. As one of the first people our patients meet or speak to, you will play an important role in helping patients access the right care and providing a welcoming, professional and compassionate service. This is a varied role within a busy GP practice, combining reception, care navigation and general administrative duties. No two days are the same, and you will work closely with our GPs, nurses, dispensary and wider practice team. About the role Your duties will include: Welcoming patients and visitors and providing a friendly and professional reception service. Answering telephone calls and dealing with patient enquiries promptly and courteously. Helping patients access the most appropriate clinician, service or source of advice. Processing appointment requests and supporting patients to use our online services and triage systems. Booking, changing and cancelling appointments accurately. Registering new patients and maintaining accurate patient information. Updating patient records and entering information accurately onto the practice clinical system. Responding to patient enquiries face-to-face, by telephone and electronically. Supporting GPs, nurses and other members of the clinical team with administrative tasks. Maintaining patient confidentiality and complying with GDPR, Caldicott and practice policies. Dealing sensitively and professionally with patients who may be distressed, anxious or frustrated. Helping to maintain a clean, tidy and welcoming reception and waiting-room environment. Participating in practice meetings, training and quality-improvement activities. Undertaking other reasonable duties appropriate to the role.
